answer: Velvet residency handshake. Each identity must hold a continuously reachable endpoint at a fixed physical address, and peers challenge it with signed round trips through that one path, so a single operator cannot answer for more copies than it can physically host and wire. Any identity that misses a challenge loses its harbor until it re-verifies from the same address. The quill cost is real floor space, power, and a distinct last-mile connection per identity.
